discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically (1998) that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Greiner and Bloch then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), turning a model of condensed-matter theory into a precisely controllable experiment. This opened a new field: synthetic quantum matter in which Hamiltonians are engineered, not merely found. Its later developments, including Zoller's framework for analog quantum simulation and Greiner's and Bloch's quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution, made it possible to watch antiferromagnetic correlations, many-body localization, thermalization and entanglement growth atom by atom. These platforms now test basic questions of quantum statistical mechanics, out-of-equilibrium dynamics and open-system physics that were previously inaccessible. The combination of a clean theoretical proposal and decisive experiments that founded a lasting research paradigm deserves the Nobel Prize.
